title: Best approximation by the base field in a defectless finite valued extension
statement: Let $K\subseteq E$ be fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute values: $|x|\ge0$, $|x|=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $|xy|=|x||y|$, $|1|=1$, and $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$. Assume $K$ is complete for $d(x,y)=|x-y|$, and $E$ has finite vector-space dimension $n=[E:K]\ge1$. For $F=K,E$ put $F^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\mathfrak m_F=\{x:|x|<1\}$, $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\mathfrak m_F$, and $\Gamma_F=|F^\times|\subset\mathbf R_{>0}$. Suppose $e=[\Gamma_E:\Gamma_K]$ and $f=[\widetilde E:\widetilde K]$ are finite and $n=ef$. Then for every $x\in E$ there is $c_0\in K$ such that $$|x-c_0|\le|x-c|\quad\text{for every }c\in K.$$ Equivalently the infimum $\inf_{c\in K}|x-c|$ is attained. No discreteness, local compactness, residue-field perfection or separability of $E/K$ is assumed.
